message.reasoning_content:
The description model is already recorded; claims c1/c2 exist. Nothing new to add — I can refine risk_map with quantitative detail relevant to experiments. Record a brief update supporting experiment design: emphasize that a CPU-simulatable probe can reproduce the float32 accumulation order exactly, and that measuring weight distortion and final output suffices.

Add useful detail: error propagation estimate — ulp of ~1.6e4 in fp32 is ~2^-9 ≈ 0.002; per-anchor distance error up to ~1e-3, -16*d change ~0.016 → weight relative change ~1.6%. Multiple independent accumulators: anchor_norm, query_norm, dot each contribute. Note that true distances d_i ~ 32*(0.0156)^2 ≈ 0.0078, -16d ≈ -0.125, weights ∈ ~[0.88,1]. Note that because weights are all close to each other (ratio near 1), the normalized mean is a near-uniform average of values; distortion of weights by ~1-2% relative likely shifts the mean by far less than 5%. This is important context for the skeptic: the failure may not exceed tolerance. Also that c1's O(10%) weight distortion estimate is likely overstated.
